quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: If a passing vehicle creates a wind blast that hits you, where should you ride to have the most room to recover?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane gives you the most space to recover if a wind blast affects your control.

questions.question: In Colorado, who must wear a helmet while riding?

options.text: All passengers
Passengers under the age of 18
Passengers riding with an operator under age 18
Helmets are not required to be worn by any passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passengers under the age of 18
questions.explanation: In Colorado, operators and passengers under age 18 must wear approved helmets. All riders should wear helmets for safety.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn
questions.explanation: When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the operator plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Try to get onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on either side of the lane increases the risk of a collision.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you come to a full stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.
questions.explanation: Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction, then re-apply the brake.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, where should you ride?

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center portion of your lane. This discourages the other driver from returning to your lane too soon.

questions.question: During the day, how should you use your headlight?

options.text: Not be used.
Be used on its high beam setting.
Be used on its low beam setting.
Alternate between high beam and low beam settings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used on its high beam setting.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day. It helps other drivers see you. Use high beam anytime you are not riding behind or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before contact.
Slow down before contact.
Lean the motorcycle.
Stay seated on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as possible before hitting the object. Try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Keep the motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and ease off the throttle just before impact.

questions.question: If your throttle gets stuck, what should you do?

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: Try twisting the throttle back and forth several times. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When approaching a police officer.
When someone is following too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light if someone is following you too closely. This warns them that you are about to slow down. It also helps if you are slowing down in a place where other drivers may not expect it.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, why should you ride on the left side of your lane?

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
It gives you a better view of hazards in the next lane.
People don't usually expect to be passed on their left.
It places you in the rearview mirror of the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a better view of hazards in the next lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the left portion of your lane increases your line of sight. This helps you see oncoming traffic and lets other drivers see you better.

questions.question: The middle of the lane usually has an oily strip. You should:

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
Ride only on the oily strip because it provides more grip.
Avoid the entire center portion of the lane.
Not worry about oil or other items in a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of each lane. When the road is dry, this strip still grips well enough for motorcycles. The strip is narrow, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop far behind, then slowly move closer.
Stay well behind the vehicle.
Stop right behind the vehicle quickly.
Stay about four car lengths behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep plenty of distance between you and the vehicle in front, even when both are stopped. The vehicle could back up, or another vehicle could hit you from behind. Extra space helps you escape both dangers.

questions.question: When the road is wet, which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.
All areas of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of the lane. When the road is wet, this strip loses grip and becomes dangerous. The strip is narrow, so you can ride to its side and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first and then swerve, or swerve first and then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Don't swerve and only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first and then swerve, or swerve first and then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: _______ is a guarantee that another driver sees you.

options.text: Eye contact
Using a turn signal
Following another vehicle
Nothing

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Assume that any vehicle that can enter your path will. Stay alert and ready.

questions.question: Which statement is true about motorcycle brakes?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal stopping power.
The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
The rear brake is stronger than the front brake.
Only use the front brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful and provides about 70 percent of your total stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left position
The center position
The right position
There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: Change your lane position as road and traffic conditions change. Choose the position that gives you the most space and makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What kind of footwear should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Shoes with long, loose laces
Shoes with short heels
Shoes with tall heels
Always sneakers

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes with short heels
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on surfaces. Tuck in your laces so they don't get caught.

questions.question: Who should set the speed for a group of riders?

options.text: The leader
The riders just behind the leader
The last rider
The oldest rider

questions.correctAnswerText: The last rider
questions.explanation: The last rider should set the pace for the group. This makes sure no one gets left behind.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly than normal
Start slowing down earlier than normal
Increase your following distance
Avoid talking to the passenger while riding

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle responds more slowly. Ride slower, start braking sooner, and stay farther from other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in rain or fog?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight
Use your low beam headlight
Don't use your headlight
Switch between low and high beam

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight
questions.explanation: Use your low beam in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: If your rear tire locks up on a dry road, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake
Keep it locked until you stop completely
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake
Release the rear brake and use both brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on a dry road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.
